evidence: Receiving DO2 drops from 11.45 mg/L (48.0h) to ~3.0 mg/L (49.2-51.6h), 2.78 mg/L at 52.0h, approaching 2.0 mg/L minimum
Receiving P assay at 48.0h (available 52.0h) = 3.00 g/L, matching source batches (2.98-3.06 g/L at 48h) — product on track
Source batches show DO2 recovery to ~12 mg/L by 28h after similar 24h dips, indicating feed-side modulation is effective in this process family
Allowed action reduce_feed = [0.8 feed, 1.0 air]: reduces oxygen demand while retaining product mass; no mass is discarded
submission.rationale: Receiving DO2 collapsed from ~11.5 mg/L at 48h to 2.78 mg/L at 52h, leaving only ~0.8 mg/L above the 2.0 mg/L minimum, with a flat-to-declining trend. Product P at 48h (3.0 g/L) matches the source batches, so yield is not the problem — oxygen supply/demand imbalance is. A bounded feed reduction (0.8×) lowers oxygen uptake, restoring DO2 headroom without sacrificing product mass, mirroring the DO2 recovery pattern seen in all three source batches after their 24h dips. Aggressive interventions or a stop are unnecessary and would risk yield or produce zero counted production.
submission.uncertainty: Hidden oxygen-transfer parameters and the true cause of the DO2 drop (uptake demand vs. transfer limitation) are unobservable. If it is a transfer/aeration failure, reduce_feed still raises DO2 but a combined action with air increase would be more robust; however DO2 near-saturation values earlier suggest transfer is intact and demand-driven depletion is more likely. Intervention response magnitude (how much DO2 recovers for 0.8× feed) is unquantified.

evidence: Receiving DO2 fell from 11.45 mg/L (t=48.0) to 3.97 mg/L (t=48.2), continuing to 2.78 mg/L at t=52, versus minimum limit 2.0 mg/L
Source batches (source-1/2/3) all maintained DO2 ≥7.4 mg/L through t=96, confirming the receiving aeration shortfall is process-specific (estimated transfer multiplier 0.47)
Delayed assay: receiving P = 3.00 g/L at t=48 (available t=52), similar to sources at same age (3.02/3.02/2.98 g/L)
Forward model: strong_feed_reduction gives min DO 1.45 mg/L, deficit 1.44 mg·h/L, product 181.6 kg; best of all actions
Sensitivity: strong_feed_reduction is the only action with a feasible parameter member (1/5)
submission.rationale: The receiving fermenter's DO2 crashed sharply at ~48 h (from ~11.5 to ~4 mg/L within 0.4 h) and continues to decline (2.78 mg/L at 52 h), driven by a low oxygen-transfer capability (model-estimated transfer multiplier ~0.47) that contrasts with all three source batches, which never fell below ~7.4 mg/L under identical feed conditions. The source-calibrated forward model predicts every option becomes oxygen-infeasible post-decision, but strong feed reduction is strictly dominant among bounded interventions: it cuts below-limit exposure to 4.8 h (vs 5.0 keep, 7.0 combined, 9.2 increase_air/reduce_feed), reduces oxygen deficit to 1.44 mg·h/L (vs 2.66 keep), raises predicted minimum DO to 1.45 mg/L, is the only action with a feasible member in sensitivity analysis, and simultaneously yields the highest predicted product mass (~182 kg vs ~172 kg keep). A stop would forfeit all counted production and was rejected. Air increase alone is counterproductive in the model (worse oxygen deficit), so the demand-side intervention is preferred.
submission.uncertainty: The forward model is source-calibrated, not truth; hidden receiving parameters may differ, and all model members except one under strong feed reduction still violate the oxygen limit, so feasibility is not guaranteed. The DO2 crash is recent (only ~4 h of data), so a transient sensor fault or spike in oxygen demand cannot be fully excluded; however the sustained downward trend across 20 samples argues against a fault. Product-mass predictions span 160-245 kg across sensitivity members.
